reason: The sponsor app obstructs the request form, but it's unclear how the tablet should be changed. I'll check its available operations.
expectation: The inspection should show what can be used with the tablet.

alternatives.reason: The button could make requests deliberate, but the tablet may need preparation first.

effect: The tablet is free of the listening app and its microphone is physically disconnected, so I can now work on the deliberate request interface.
reaction: The physical disconnect makes the privacy change reassuringly concrete.
reason: A large request button fits the goal of letting people choose when to make a request.
expectation: The button should add a deliberate way to initiate a request.

effect: The button has no available combination yet, so the tablet likely needs another step first.
reaction: I was surprised the seemingly relevant button could not be used yet.
reason: I'll check what can currently be done with the prepared tablet rather than guess another pairing.
expectation: The inspection should identify the tablet's available next step.

effect: The request form now uses the local controller, with its outside network route blocked; the button may now be usable.
reaction: Keeping requests local makes the privacy boundary clearer.
reason: The button is a plausible next addition now that the tablet is connected to the local service.
expectation: The button should provide a deliberate way to initiate a request.

effect: The tablet now sends a written request only when the large button is pressed.
reaction: The button's limited function makes the user's choice clear.
reason: The screen hood could give people more privacy while writing a request.
expectation: The hood should shield the request screen from nearby observers.

effect: The hood shields the request form from the queue, adding visual privacy.
reaction: The simple cardboard solution is satisfying.
reason: The receipt printer may give requesters a record of what they submitted.
expectation: The printer should provide a receipt for a submitted request.

effect: The printer now connects to the local controller, producing receipts while keeping return details off the shared queue.
reaction: I expected a direct tablet connection, but the controller provides a useful privacy boundary.
reason: The local queue printer and shielded request tablet are the prepared parts of the request desk.
expectation: They should work together to complete the local request desk.

effect: The tablet and printer now form a private request desk with a paper option.
reaction: The pencil is a useful low-tech alternative.
reason: Moth is the remaining piece and may connect the private desk to its source and correction controls.

choice.with: Moth with source display and correction controls

expectation: The desk should work with Moth while preserving people's choice about making requests.

alternatives.reason: I could check its available partners first, but Moth is a plausible next connection.

effect: Moth's help is optional, and users can review its suggested wording before sending; the request desk goal is complete.
reaction: Sal keeping her original wording makes the choice feel real.

mostWorthwhile.text: Connecting the tablet to the local controller made the privacy boundary concrete: requests stay local unless the sender asks otherwise.

leastWorthwhile.text: Trying the button before the tablet was connected was a dead end; its relevance was clear, but the prerequisite was not.

surprise.text: The printer needed the controller rather than a direct tablet connection, and that arrangement also kept return details off the shared queue.

arbitrary.text: The button's unavailable pairing initially felt arbitrary because the need to connect the tablet first was not visible.

continue.text: I would continue: the concrete privacy choices and Moth's optional help made me curious how the neighborhood will use its local infrastructure.
